Here's what I found about using `gh gei migrate-repo` with local archive files via `--git-archive-path` and `--metadata-archive-path`:

## The short answer: These flags don't exist for `gh gei migrate-repo`

The `--git-archive-path` and `--metadata-archive-path` options you're looking for are **not currently supported** by the `gh gei migrate-repo` command. This was raised as a feature request in [GitHub issue #1196](https://github.com/github/gh-gei/issues/1196).

## What you need to do instead

Currently, if you already have Git and metadata archives on your local machine, you have to work around the missing feature. In some scenarios, you may already have the Git archive and metadata archive on your local machine and want to import it. This is supported—but you have to upload the file to a blob storage provider yourself, generate a URL for the file, and then call migrate-repo with the `--git-archive-url` and `--metadata-archive-url` arguments.

The requested enhancement would simplify this: the process of importing an already-existing archive would be easier if you could pass a `--git-archive-path` and `--metadata-archive-path` instead, and ask the CLI to upload it to blob storage for you and generate a URL.

## Practical options

**Option 1 — Use archive URLs (the current supported path):**
Upload your local archives to blob storage (Azure Blob Storage or AWS S3), generate URLs (with a SAS token for Azure or a pre-signed URL for S3), then run something like:

```
gh gei migrate-repo --github-source-org SOURCE_ORG --source-repo REPO \
  --github-target-org TARGET_ORG \
  --git-archive-url <URL> --metadata-archive-url <URL> --wait
```

This mirrors the community example: `gh gei migrate-repo --github-source-org $GHES_ORGANIZATION --source-repo $GHES_REPO --github-target-org Deep-Space-9 --git-archive-url <URL> --metadata-archive-url <URL> --wait`

You can use Azure Blob Storage or AWS S3 to store the archives; it is recommended that the archives are stored privately, so in order for GEI to access the archives, you will need to provide a URL with a SAS token.

**Option 2 — Use GitHub-owned storage (`--use-github-storage`):**
A newer feature lets you skip managing your own blob storage entirely. Make sure you are running version v1.9.0 or greater of the gei or bbs2gh extension, then simply pass the `--use-github-storage` option to your `gh gei` or `gh bbs2gh` commands. The CLI will then be performing migrations using GitHub-owned storage. Note this was introduced because in the past, to migrate from GHES, Bitbucket Server, and Bitbucket Data Center, an external storage provider was required. With GitHub-owned storage for GEI, this is no longer a requirement—migrations can now be performed with archives uploaded directly to GitHub.com.

## A note on `bbs2gh` (Bitbucket)

If you happen to be migrating from **Bitbucket** rather than GitHub Enterprise Server/GitHub.com, note that the `bbs2gh` sibling command *does* have a local archive path option. One user described a two-step flow where the export generates a .tar file which is manually copied to the local machine, and then a second `gh bbs2gh migrate-repo` call is made with the `--archive-path`, `--github-org`, `--github-repo` and `--aws-bucket-name` arguments. However, this is `--archive-path` on `bbs2gh`, not `--git-archive-path`/`--metadata-archive-path` on `gei`.

## Tip

To check the exact options available in your installed version, run:

`gh gei migrate-repo --help` will list all the options available for the migrate-repo command. Since the GEI extension is updated weekly, it's worth verifying whether the requested `--git-archive-path`/`--metadata-archive-path` support has been added in a newer release.
